mcp.name: Name
mcp.levelHint: Level at which this definition is stored (app/user/project/prjusr, each = `<level root>/capability/mcps/<name>.json`). Same name across levels = most specific wins, whole-entry override (prjusr > project > user > app); only one takes effect.
mcp.nameRequired: MCP Server name cannot be empty
mcp.nameFormat: MCP Server name must start with a letter and contain only letters, digits and underscores
mcp.connectorRequired: Runtime or Server URL is required (at least one)
mcp.confirmDelete: Are you sure to delete this MCP Server?
mcp.runtimePlaceholder: e.g. npx (executable/interpreter; a path with spaces goes in whole)
mcp.argsPlaceholder: One arg per line (passed verbatim, no quote parsing)
mcp.transportHint: http = Streamable HTTP; sse = legacy SSE (2024-11-05); stdio = local subprocess (runtime/args); auto = url → http, runtime only → stdio
mcp.urlIgnoredHint: stdio spawns the subprocess via runtime only; the Server URL will be ignored
mcp.isolateHint: Isolation key = (instance + project working directory): the same server gets an independent connection/subprocess per instance and per project. stdio defaults ON (a single pipe cannot process calls concurrently — sharing blocks them); http/sse point at an existing process on a fixed port (not spawned by us) and therefore **cannot truly be isolated** — default OFF. No isolation = one shared connection for all instances (built once at construction, reused for the whole lifetime, never reclaimed by the idle sweep); isolate = lazily create a connection/subprocess per (instance + project), reclaimed after ~60s idle and re-spawned on the next call.
mcp.sandboxHint: agentbox restricts the server subprocess file access to the trust dirs (readable/writable, recursive) of the project security page; applies to stdio & spawn only (http/sse point at a fixed-port process not spawned by us — neither isolation nor sandboxing is possible). The sandbox does NOT depend on isolation — no need to enable per-instance isolation first. Unset = no sandbox (default); an empty allow-list means no policy is sent (= none applied, not an all-reject).
mcp.sandboxEmptyHint: Server-level sandbox: effective only when the switch is on + transport is stdio + the trust-dir list is non-empty; an empty trust-dir config means NO isolation is applied (it is NOT an all-reject) and is independent of per-instance isolation (no need to enable it first); only the executor-level sandbox rejects everything when its trust dirs are empty.
mcp.sandboxStdioOnly: Only stdio & spawn MCP servers can be sandboxed; http/sse point at a fixed port — neither isolation nor sandboxing is possible
mcp.hotToolsEmpty: No tools for this server (disabled / not connected / no tools)
mcp.loadToolsHint: Click "Load tools" to read this server's tool list
mcp.envPlaceholder: One K=V per line, e.g. NODE_ENV=production (values support %VAR% and ${VAR} expansion)
mcp.headersPlaceholder: One K=V per line, e.g. Authorization=Bearer xxx

toolAsync.pageHint: User-level config (usr db): all tools grouped by MCP; unconfigured tools follow the contract defaults. Saved changes take effect immediately.
toolAsync.modeHint: Four modes — Async only: return task_id immediately and run in background; Sync only: block for the result; Auto async: move to background at the threshold (no re-run); Manual async: arbitration at the threshold + a “to async” icon on the tool message.
toolAsync.thresholdHint: Trigger async arbitration at this many seconds (Auto/Manual modes only; empty = contract default; 0 / -1 = no threshold, wait forever until cancelled).
toolAsync.contractTooltip: This tool's contract defaults — mode: {mode}; threshold: {threshold}; timeout: {timeout}
toolAsync.advancedHint: The subprocess is killed at this limit; backgrounded tasks are bound by it too. Empty = fall back to global (unset); 0 / -1 = no limit (wait forever, user can cancel).
toolAsync.descAlways: Always async: returns task_id immediately and runs in background
toolAsync.descNever: Always sync: blocks for the result; timeout asks the user
toolAsync.descAuto: Auto async: moves to background at the threshold (no re-run)
toolAsync.descManual: Manual async: arbitration at the threshold + a “to async” icon on the tool message
toolAsync.hardTimeoutNotApplicable: hard_timeout is not wired for dir-node tools and has no effect (mode / threshold still apply)
toolAsync.touchFilesHint: On = this tool touches files, so a checkpoint is taken before it runs; Off = it does not touch files → the call is passed through without a checkpoint (saves ~8–9 git processes). Defaults by origin: built-in tools only filesys_run / script_run touch files, other built-ins do not; dir-node / third-party tools default to touching (conservative). The end-of-turn checkpoint is always kept (a final image always exists); a wrong flag only coarsens checkpoint granularity (surrounding checkpoints remain, git diff consistency checks still apply) — safety is not lost.

toolSandbox.pageHint: User-level config (usr db): one switch per executor category (core / desktop / browser — the three self executors) controlling all tools under that executor; when enabled, agentbox restricts their file access to the trust dirs (readable/writable, recursive) of the project security page. Changes are written only when you click Save (Save is disabled when there are no changes). Unset = no isolation.
toolSandbox.empty: No isolatable executor tools scanned (core / desktop / browser)
toolSandbox.switchHint: Whether agentbox sandboxing is enabled for this executor (all its tools; unset = no isolation)
toolSandbox.thirdPartyHint: The sandbox applies per executor and only covers self tools (core / desktop / browser). Configure third-party MCP sandboxing in the MCP dialog's Runtime tab (only stdio & spawn can be isolated / sandboxed); http/sse point at an existing process on a fixed port (not spawned by us) — neither isolation nor sandboxing is possible.
toolSandbox.trustDirWarning: Sandboxing is on but the project trust dirs are empty: an empty allow-list in agentbox means deny-all, so currently **every file operation of the sandboxed executors is rejected**. Configure the readable/writable dirs first.
toolSandbox.trustDirWarningRow: Trust dirs empty → all file operations of this executor will be rejected
